issues.body:
Cargo.toml adds `crates/sparq-wrapper-shacl`, `crates/sparq-wrapper-gen` and `crates/sparq-wrapper-integration` to `[workspace] members`, but Cargo.lock is untouched by this PR and contains no `[[package]]` entry for any of them.

Verified mechanically against the PR head: parsing `[workspace].members` gives 67 crates; 64 have a matching `name = "..."` in Cargo.lock and the only three missing are exactly the three this PR adds. Cargo.lock is git-tracked and is not gitignored.

Cargo records every workspace member as a package in the lock, and it resolves the whole workspace even when a single package is selected with `-p`. With the lock stale, any `--locked` invocation aborts with "the lock file needs to be updated but --locked was passed":
  - .github/workflows/build-matrix.yml:123-124 `cargo auditable build --release --locked -p sparq-cli` / `-p sparq-server`
  - .github/workflows/feature-matrix.yml:539, 669, 735, 806, 871 `cargo fetch --locked`
  - .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml:277, 311 `cargo fetch --locked`
On the non-`--locked` lanes cargo instead rewrites Cargo.lock in place, leaving a dirty tree for any step that checks for uncommitted changes.

This is not a repo convention that dependency-less `publish = false` crates are omitted: the three comparable stub crates all carry lock entries — sparq-conformance-floors at Cargo.lock:4999, sparq-crdt at 5021, sparq-e2ee-ng at 5041 — and each was added in the PR that landed its crate.

I could not run cargo to reproduce the exact error (rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.97.1 and the sandbox rustup dir is read-only; an offline resolve on the installed 1.88.0 fails first on the `solid-oidc-verifier` git dependency of sparq-lws-core). The finding is from direct comparison of the members list against the lock, which is deterministic.
issues.fix_hint: Run `cargo metadata --format-version 1 >/dev/null` (or `cargo check --workspace`) with the pinned 1.97.1 toolchain and commit the resulting Cargo.lock. The diff should be three new `[[package]] name = "sparq-wrapper-gen" / "sparq-wrapper-integration" / "sparq-wrapper-shacl"` stanzas with `version = "0.1.0"` and no `dependencies` key, matching the shape of the sparq-conformance-floors entry at Cargo.lock:4999. Then confirm `cargo fetch --locked` exits 0.
issues.title: Three new workspace members are not in the committed Cargo.lock, breaking every `--locked` CI lane

issues.body:
Carried from rounds 1-2 at the same severity; unchanged in this round. sparq-wrapper-gen, sparq-wrapper-shacl and sparq-wrapper-integration are each a Cargo.toml with an empty `[dependencies]` plus a three-line `//!`-only lib.rs. Nothing depends on them and they export nothing, yet each is built, clippy'd and doc'd on every CI run.

The hygiene requirement asked for in round 1 was met faithfully: each README carries the `<!-- internal-stub -->` directive, a one-line what/why and the `sq-1rg2q.1` bead marker, and I re-confirmed gate-new-crate.py --dry-run (G1) PASS and check-readme-template.py --enforce 0 deviations. Residual cost only, and a maintainer call rather than a defect.

One small inconsistency with the sibling stubs: sparq-crdt/Cargo.toml and sparq-conformance-floors/Cargo.toml both set `readme = "README.md"` explicitly; the three new manifests omit it. Cargo auto-detects README.md in the package directory, so this is cosmetic and the README template gate passes either way.
issues.fix_hint: If keeping them, no action beyond stating the reservation rationale in the PR body; optionally add `readme = "README.md"` to match the sibling stub manifests. If not, drop the three members and record each planned seam as a bead, creating the crate in the PR that implements it.
issues.title: Three empty crates join the workspace with no API, no dependents, and no consumer

issues.body:
Partly resolved this round: the stale header sentence "All five proposal implementations are default-OFF" is replaced with a count-free "Implemented proposal features are default-OFF", so the comment no longer drifts as features are added. What remains is that proposed-async-events, proposed-async-node, proposed-async-store, proposed-graph-scope-events and proposed-json have no leg, so no CI lane ever builds them.

That is currently harmless and I confirmed why: check-feature-test-execution.py's C1 guard only scans `crates/*/tests/**` files with an inner `#![cfg(feature = ...)]` and `[[test]]`/`[[bench]]` `required-features` entries, and these five features gate no test target. Each gated module is a 3-line doc-comment-only file, so a build of them could not fail. Verified module sizes: the five reserved modules are 3 lines each; cardinality/codecs/graph_scope/observe/typed_focus are 232-499 lines, which independently supports SKILL.md's "every other proposal feature is implemented" claim.
issues.fix_hint: No change required now. Add each leg in the PR that lands the corresponding implementation and its tests, so C1 stays fail-closed the moment a gated test appears.
issues.title: The five reserved features have no feature-matrix leg (harmless while the modules are empty)

issues.body:
Carried from round 2, unchanged. The PR ships crates/sparq-wrapper/docs/proposed/*.md and skills/rdf-wrapper/references/*.md — 24 files carrying the same eleven facts. They are now complete and consistent in substance (I verified both indexes cover all 11 features with no unlinked or dangling page, and distinct.md is byte-identical in both trees), but the wording still diverges per page: docs/proposed/graph_scope_events.md says "Reserved implementation: `src/proposed/graph_scope_events.rs`" while references/graph_scope_events.md says "Reserved for a future implementation behind the default-off `proposed-graph-scope-events` feature". Every future proposal landing must touch both trees in lockstep, and the round-2 omission of distinct from both indexes was an early instance of that drift.

Worth noting rdf-wrapper is the only skill in the repo with a `references/` subdirectory, so this layout is new convention rather than an existing pattern.
issues.fix_hint: Consider collapsing to one status table — a single section in skills/rdf-wrapper/SKILL.md, or one page listing all eleven features with a status column — and have crates/sparq-wrapper/README.md link to it, instead of 24 single-fact files kept in sync by hand.
issues.title: Two parallel status trees duplicate the same per-feature status in different wording

verdict.summary:
Both round-2 findings are genuinely closed. SKILL.md:84-90 now correctly states proposed-distinct is implemented as inherent Dataset methods in the crate root (verified against src/lib.rs:154-184 and tests/wrapper.rs); it no longer contradicts SKILL.md:122 or the crate README. Both status indexes now cover all 11 features; I resolved every relative link in skills/rdf-wrapper/** and crates/sparq-wrapper/**: 0 broken, 0 unlinked page, 0 dangling entry. Gates I could run all PASS: gate-new-crate.py (G1), check-readme-template.py --enforce (0/67), gate-api-skill.py (G2), coverage-presence.py (42 ok/0 fail). The stale 'All five proposal implementations' comment is fixed, Cargo.toml's 11 features match SKILL.md's 11, and every 'Reserved implementation: src/proposed/X.rs' page names a file that now exists.

One blocker remains, pre-existing in the PR since round 1 but missed by both prior rounds: Cargo.toml adds three workspace members and Cargo.lock was not regenerated. Verified mechanically — 64 of 67 members appear in Cargo.lock; the three missing are exactly sparq-wrapper-shacl, sparq-wrapper-gen, sparq-wrapper-integration. Cargo resolves the whole workspace even under -p, so every --locked lane fails: build-matrix.yml:123-124, feature-matrix.yml (5x cargo fetch --locked), supply-chain.yml:277,311. The comparable stub crates (sparq-crdt, sparq-conformance-floors, sparq-e2ee-ng) all have lock entries, so this is a missed step, not a convention.

Progress is 'regressing' strictly per the stated scale (a new finding above the severity of anything carried). Qualitatively the fix commit is good: it closed the blocker and the major and introduced no new false claim.

Limitation: I could not compile — rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.97.1 and the sandbox rustup dir is read-only; an offline resolve on 1.88.0 aborts on the solid-oidc-verifier git dep. The lock finding is from file comparison, not a build. No hostile content, no new dependency, no unsafe, no crypto/ZK/MPC surface.
